reports.title: Iris Fordham: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The poor quality of recording clinical records impeded the Trust's governance processes, in that the author of a serious incident investigation was unable to rely on clear evidence to understand why essential actions were not carried out in Ms [name redacted] care.
The Trust failed to complete a falls risk assessment of Ms Fordham.
The consequence of (2) was that no falls care plan was completed.

The fact that the failures at (2) & (3) were not detected and remediated by successive clinical staff members suggests that they did not read essential parts of the clinical record when providing care. The cumulative failings, on the part of multiple healthcare professionals suggests a culture of indifference inimical to the provision of safe and effective practice.
The Trust has not considered any step to resolve individual failings in care through disciplinary or regulatory channels.
concerns.hazard: lack of disciplinary or regulatory action

reports.title: Thomas Doyle: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The trust's clinical records were of a particularly poor standard which impeded the Trust's governance investigation and the inquest investigation in determining what, if any consideration was given to the possibility that Mr Doyle was suffering from an infection
The Trust's failure to commence a diagnostic pathway to investigate sepsis when clearly indicated on Mr [name redacted] admission, as required by both local policy and national guidance
concerns.hazard: failure to initiate sepsis diagnostic pathway

reports.title: David Morris: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The CQC has confirmed that they are reviewing this case, and will consider what further action should be taken, and whether any monitoring of the trust, or regulatory response, is required.
promises.summary: CQC reviewing case and considering monitoring or regulatory response

promises.quote: be able to check the wording in their specific product information to ensure the appropriate advice on checking for leaks is present.
promises.summary: Check product information for leak warnings

concerns.quote: Mr [name redacted] diagnosis and treatment for cancer was delayed due to poor organisation and communication at the Trust.

During the evening of 3rd May 2022 going into the early hours of 4th May 2022, Doctors and nurses failed to identify the extent of Mr [name redacted] gastrostomy leak and the onset of sepsis. After identifying symptoms of sepsis, staff failed to treat and escalate Mr [name redacted] care resulting in a delay of three and a half hours before a medical review commenced emergency treatment.

During Mr [name redacted] ward-based treatment on 3 & 4th May 2022 clinical records were either of a poor standard or were non-existent. The absence of clear records impeded the effective investigation of this death by the Trust's governance teams and the Coroner.

The initial serious investigation report into Mr [name redacted] death was unfit for purpose. The report to investigate or even identify the Registrar who reviewed Mr Morris on the evening of 3rd May 2022. Since then, no effective review has been undertaken by the Trust upon how this deficient report gained executive approval.

The Trust did not have effective controlled drug management systems in place to detect a prolonged and persistent course of conduct from an employed nurse who was stealing and self- administering controlled drugs in the workplace.
concerns.hazard: lack of controlled drug management systems
